title: 10-minute lightning tech demo outline for sellers (sketch)
body:
Purpose:
- Give SEs a compact, repeatable 10-minute technical demo for early-stage evaluation calls (pilot qualification / initial architecture).
- Emphasis: show predictable latency, cost levers, and safe fallbacks rather than deep model internals.
- Keep it skippable: three tight pivot points so seller can expand if buyer asks deeper questions.

Primary audience:
- Integration architects, platform engineers, engineering leads evaluating inference choices for product features.
- 10–15 minute window in a discovery or pilot kickoff where we need to demonstrate credibility and an easy on-ramp.

Outcome we want after the call:
- Customer agrees to a pilot scope (<= 2 feature endpoints, < 500k tokens/week) or a follow-up deep technical session.
- Seller captures VM/cluster constraints and regulatory needs for Private/Dedicated sizing.

Flow (0–10 minutes):
- 0:00–0:30 — Quick context + credibility (scripted): "We help teams run inference with predictable latency, cost, and fallbacks across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- 0:30–1:15 — One-slide architecture: show API -> Smart Router -> Serving Runtime -> Fallbacks (tiny diagram). Call out: autoscaling, KV caching, and quantization profiles.
- 1:15–3:00 — Live 1: simple generate + streaming: demo a short prompt (e.g., summarize customer guidelines) showing streaming tokens and trace in Console (latency token times).
    - Talking points: per-token latency, how streaming reduces time-to-first-byte, what we measure (p50/p95).
- 3:00–5:00 — Live 2: latency vs batch demo (scripted): show same workload hitting Hosted and Dedicated model variant (or emulate higher qps). Explain batching tradeoffs and the cost delta.
    - Show a quick table: tokens/sec, cost/token estimate, and observed 95th percentile latency.
- 5:00–6:20 — Quick routing & fallback walkthrough: change route to cheaper-compatible model variant (quantized) when capacity constrained and show an automatic fallback to a compatible variant.
    - Give the seller one-liner: "We keep your app online by routing to compatible variants — fallbacks are policy-driven and observable."
- 6:20–8:00 — Observability snapshot: Console demo (latency heatmap, token-level breakdown, per-route cost). Highlight alert: quality regression tied to prompt set (show a simple eval card).
- 8:00–9:00 — Security & deployment modes: quick bullets about Dedicated commitments, VPC/private control plane, and KMS/HSM options.
- 9:00–10:00 — Next steps and ask: propose 30-min pilot-handshake session; capture infra constraints and sample prompt set.

Key slides / artifacts to prepare (one-liners sellers should memorize):
- Slide A: "Predictable latency with fallback guarantees" (diagram + SLO language).
- Slide B: "Cost levers: batching, caching, quantization" (3 mini examples w/ ballpark numbers).
- Slide C: "Pilot handshake: what we need from you in 30 min" (sample prompts, traffic shape, security needs).

Demo scripts (concise copy to paste into demo machine):
- Stream demo prompt: "Summarize the following customer-facing guideline in 2 bullets: <paste short policy>"
- Batching demo sequence: fire 10 concurrent requests via curl loop; switch routing policy to 'dedicated' and show p95 drop.
- Fallback demo: toggle policy (button in Console) to route to a quantized variant and show a short dev log message indicating fallback.

Objection handling (quick bullets):
- "What about quality when you quantize?" -> "We provide model-variant profiling and auto-regression alerts; quantization profiles are recommended per workload and validated against saved prompt sets."
- "How do we guarantee SLA?" -> "Reserved Dedicated capacity with burst capacity options + routing fallback policies; we can commit to p95 latency targets for a pinned model version."
- "Data privacy for private deployments?" -> "Private control plane and on-prem package; KMS/HSM integration; we support audit logs per-token if required for compliance."

Quick technical checkpoints (things seller must capture during the call):
- Sample prompt set (2–5 examples) and expected output style.
- QPS and acceptable p95 latency (ms).
- Throughput burndown: token length distribution (p50/p95 tokens per request).
- Security boundary: need for VPC or HSM, any regulatory must-haves.

Canary + Pilot handshake (short checklist sellers can paste into email):
- Pilot scope (features/endpoints): __
- Traffic estimate (daily tokens / peak qps): __
- Sample prompts attached: Y/N
- Preferred deployment: hosted | dedicated | private
- Compliance needs (SOC2 / HIPAA / other): __
- Next call: 30-min pilot-handshake (link)

Notes to self / rough TODOs (internal only):
- Add a 1-minute riff about "cost predictability" with a tiny worked example for LLM selection. (Marisol)
- Confirm that Console demo account has two model variants preloaded and a recorded traffic script for reliable demo (Ethan).
- Create a short animated gif for fallback toggle to drop into the slide deck (Samir).

Unresolved questions to decide before we ship:
- Do we show Hosted vs Dedicated as live or emulate Dedicated with a labelled synthetic run? (ops constraints)
- Which three metrics should be visible by default in the tiny Console view (p50, p95, cost/token?).

References / links to stash in the deck:
- Confluence: GTM/lightning-demo-guidelines
- Jira: GTM-4127 demo-scripts and checklist
- Slack thread: #g2m-demo-runbook (search: fallback-gif)

Speaker prompts (two-line cues for sellers):
- "If you care about latency at the 95th percentile, we can show you how routing + caching keeps p95 stable as load spikes."
- "If you want to prioritize cost, we can route to compatible quantized variants — we'll run an eval against your prompt set first."

Handy one-liners to finish:
- "We focus on serving: predictable latency, transparent costs, and safe fallbacks so your product stays online while you tune for quality."

Version history:
- 2025-11-02 initial sketch
- 2026-02-15 demo script tweaks after SE dry-run
- 2026-03-10 updated canary checklist and added speaker prompts

Slack note (copy for #g2m to announce):
- "New 10-min lightning tech demo outline is up for review — Priya R. added demo scripts; Ethan has a task to ensure the demo account is ready. Feedback welcome, tagging Marisol for cost numbers."

(End of draft)
